scope: Official data.police.uk API semantics, limits and fail-closed parcel safeguards

rows.observed: street-level crime and stop-search locations are approximate rather than exact incident coordinates
rows.source: data.police.uk official street-level crime and stop-search documentation
rows.effect: API coordinates cannot prove an incident occurred inside the parcel

rows.observed: latitude and longitude select the nearest predefined location and return crimes recorded there
rows.effect: nearest-location results cannot be relabelled as exact parcel matches

rows.observed: persistent_id is the 64-character stable crime identifier while API id is not guaranteed to remain stable
rows.effect: deduplication uses persistent_id and never API id alone

rows.observed: location_type distinguishes Force and BTP and BTP locations fall within territorial force boundaries
rows.effect: Force and BTP records require persistent-id deduplication

rows.observed: the official API exposes crimes that could not be mapped to a location through a separate force and month endpoint
rows.effect: missing coordinates cannot become zero crime

rows.observed: limit is 15 requests per second with burst 30 and excess requests return HTTP 429
rows.effect: 429 triggers bounded backoff and cannot become an empty result

rows.observed: custom areas above 10000 records return 503 and GET requests above 4094 characters return 400
rows.source: data.police.uk official street-level crime and outcomes documentation
rows.effect: 400 and 503 fail closed; complex polygons use bounded POST or subdivision

rows.observed: exact parcel coordinates, API responses, reconciliation and three final SHA256 values are absent
rows.effect: score remains null
